learning: If slalom and s-bend losses fall below 1.0 per run with oscillation at or below 0.3, earlier sensing is working and the next step is gain or base_speed tuning for progress. If losses persist with oscillation rising, the forward offset is causing overshoot. Compare the first-loss bend and max_error against iteration 2.
notes: Iteration 2 controller kept unchanged so the race isolates the forward sensor shift from y 0.04 m to y 0.06 m on the 10 cm span and 12 cm track.
rationale: The Builder's proposal is the iteration 2 baseline (10 cm span, 12 cm wheel_track, 12 mm footprints, 0.8 kg) with the sensor row moved forward from y 0.04 m to y 0.06 m. Iteration 2 is the best result so far (score 124.6). It cut oval line losses to 0.05 per run, but slalom stayed at 1.0 and s-bend at 0.9, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.064 m. Iteration 3 showed that wheel_track 0.10 m removed oval losses but cut oval progress from 0.51 to 0.14, and slalom losses did not change. The drivetrain is therefore not the fix, so the track returns to 0.12 m. The forward shift is the one new variable. To isolate it, I keep the iteration 2 controller exactly (kp 1.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.0, last_direction, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2]) rather than retuning gains at the same time. I expect earlier sensing to reduce slalom and s-bend line losses. The risk is more oval oscillation, which was 0.27 at y 0.04 m.
